Oracle Cloud free tier requires 95th percentile CPU utilization above 20% or they'll shut off your server; had to set up a cronjob to periodically spike CPU to 100% to avoid this.
Signed up for Oracle Cloud's always-free tier and got 4 VM.Standard.A1.Flex instances running fine for a couple years, though heard tales of others getting instances/accounts deleted for idle usage.
Oracle Cloud reclaims idle Always Free compute resources after 7 days of low utilization, but will also ban accounts for over-utilizing free tier resources like the 10TB bandwidth allotment.
After moving to Oracle Cloud free tier, received email requiring migration to pay-as-you-go since blog had near-zero traffic, threatening to stop idle compute instances after 7 days.
Tried out Oracle Cloud free tier running an IPFS node (CPU and bandwidth heavy) and got account banned with no recourse: 'Easy come, easy go.'
Used Oracle Cloud Always Free ARM instance for about 3 years with only two ~1 minute outages; 'For the cost, I am not complaining.'
Oracle Cloud free tier offers a 4x vCPU / 24 GiB ARM Ampere VPS plus 10TB bandwidth included, which is enormously generous compared to AWS pricing for similar bandwidth.
Zoom chose Oracle Cloud for infrastructure, reportedly due to lower bandwidth costs than AWS and Azure making it cheaper for transfer-heavy services.

Using Oracle Cloud for over a year running Jenkins CI, MySQL, and a Minecraft server: 'Working flawlessly with ssh, out of the box. It is FAR simpler to manage than AWS in my opinion. There is no catch.'
Oracle Cloud DNS outage (built on the former Dyn DNS stack) caused widespread DNS failures affecting Zoom and other services relying on it.

OCI once deleted every single one of our production servers (hundreds of instances) in the middle of a work day due to an uncaught billing error; triage took over three days with significant lost customer data and financial impact. Wouldn't recommend OCI if they were the last cloud provider on earth.

OCI has severe capacity constraints and needs lots of advance notice to increase usage—'Auto scaling it ain't.' Worried that if OpenAI draws heavily from OCI hardware, other customers may struggle to get their own capacity.

In my experience OCI is still better than GCP, though AWS has been the best. Big companies like Oracle Cloud because if spend is sufficient, Oracle will build and support whatever configurations you want in any region globally.
